Samantha — thanks, answered inline below and attached the draft attestation + subprocessor inventory. Please see the short technical answers first, then the formal language in the PDF.

1) Routing / transfer witness:
- Attestation summary: For Ventura Health we can enforce a tenant-level routing policy that restricts inference work to AWS regions in the US (us-west-2, us-east-1). The runtime may route internally between AZs within those regions for availability; no EU/APAC region will be used while the policy is enabled.
- Fallback behavior: If a customer opts in to global routing, our automated fallback may select a compatible model instance in another region when same-region capacity is unavailable. For Ventura we will not enable that. The attached PDF (redwood-transfer-attestation-draft.pdf) contains the formal "transfer witness" wording we propose for your DPA annex.

2) KV cache and PHI:
- KV cache purpose: our runtime maintains per-request KV cache for model context to speed generation (not persisted long-term).
- PHI risk: KV cache stores tokenized context in memory and may be retained in hot memory for the duration of the session; it is not written to persistent disk unless customer explicitly enables long-term session store (not enabled by default).
- Mitigations / opt-outs: we offer request-level redaction hooks (pre-tokenization) and a flag to disable prefix/KV caching at the route-level. For high-sensitivity routes we recommend: enable pre-tokenization redaction, disable prefix caching, and enforce tenant-level routing to US regions.

3) KMS / keys:
- Rotation cadence: default CMK rotation is 90 days. We support customer-managed keys (CMKs) in AWS KMS and can integrate with HSM-backed providers for an additional compliance addendum.
- Key usage: model runtime encrypts persisted artifacts (if any) and secrets at rest with the configured CMK. In-flight requests are TLS-protected; ephemeral in-memory keys are used for session-level crypto.

4) Logs and retention:
- Audit logs (S3) default retention is 365 days for enterprise tenants; retention can be shortened by policy. We can provide filtered token-level traces for debugging under NDA; full token streams are considered high-sensitivity and are not retained beyond session by default.

I've also attached the current subprocessor list (subprocessors_current_list.csv) and a draft attestation PDF for legal to review.

Next steps: Samantha — please confirm whether the 90-day rotation cadence is acceptable and if Ventura requires HSM-only keys. Once confirmed, Jordan will prepare the DPA annex wording.

Kimberly Park
Director, Privacy & Controls
Redwood Inference

Kim / Rishi — thanks for the quick turn. A couple of clarifications from our side after reading the draft:

- The attestation references "ephemeral in-memory keys" for session crypto. Can you confirm whether those keys are ever materialized to swap/disk under memory pressure? If yes, we need clarification on encrypted swap policies.

- The draft states cache is not written to persistent disk "unless customer explicitly enables long-term session store" — can you point to the console/route flag name for that setting and whether it's disabled by default for new tenants? Ventura needs assurance that it will be off unless explicitly requested in writing.

- Finally, legal would like a single-sentence line that they can insert into the DPA annex describing the exporter mechanism (e.g. SCCs + US-only routing pin) — can you propose that exact sentence?

Thanks — if you can get answers by EOD today it will keep our review on schedule.

Tom Alvarez
Principal, PMC Consulting (advising Ventura Legal)

Tom — answers below (and Jordan will add the single-sentence exporter mechanism for legal):

1) Encrypted swap: Our standard runtime is configured to disable unencrypted swap for inference hosts. If the OS-level memory pressure requires swap, swap volumes are encrypted with customer CMK when tenant-level encryption is enabled. We will include a short ops note in the attestation PDF to capture that.

2) Long-term session store flag: The console flag is called "session_persistence" (route-level boolean). It is OFF by default for all new tenants and can only be turned on by an admin with explicit written approval. We'll update the attestation to name the flag and state the default.

3) Exporter mechanism sentence (draft for insertion): "Redwood Inference commits that, for Ventura Health, processing will be limited to US-based AWS regions under a tenant-level routing policy; where international transfers are necessary and agreed in writing, processing will be governed by standard EU-US data transfer safeguards (Standard Contractual Clauses or equivalent exporter mechanisms) and the parties' executed DPA annex."

Jordan — please finalize the one-line wording and the ops addendum. Samantha / Tom — let us know if that sentence works and we'll issue the final PDF + DocuSign-ready DPA annex.
